title: Naṣb Colour Guide
hero_html:
LESSON NOTES · COLOUR-CODED EXAMPLES

Naṣb: when does a word
end in fatha?

Some words in a verb sentence answer a question about the action: what, why, when, where, how. Those words take naṣb.

النَّصْب

Later (verbs)
Today we keep it simple.
  • Only past verbs (كَتَبَ) and order verbs (اُكْتُبْ). Present verbs come later.
  • Only one sign of naṣb: the fatha ـَ / ـً. The other signs come later, one chapter for each group (dual, plurals).

sections.title: A new sentence: the verb sentence
sections.sub: Last lesson the sentence started with a noun (Topic + Information). Now it starts with a verb: Verb + Doer.
sections.html:
Last lesson the sentence started with a noun (Topic + Information). Now it starts with a verb: Verb + Doer.

Verb · fixed

A past verb and an order verb are fixed (مَبْنِيّ): their ending never changes. Past: fatha كَتَبَ. Order: sukūn اُكْتُبْ.

Doer · rafʿ

The doer is who did the action. It takes rafʿ: damma, like the Topic. In an order the doer is “you”, hidden inside the verb.

A“Zayd wrote.”

Careful: the fatha on كَتَبَ is not naṣb. A past verb ends in fatha in every sentence: it is fixed. Naṣb is for nouns.

sections.title: The sign of naṣb: fatha
sections.sub: It works exactly like damma and kasra: one vowel with ال or when owned, tanween otherwise.

Iʿrāb in five questions

  1. Is it a verb or a particle? → fixed, it never changes —
  2. Topic, information, or doer? → ـُ
  3. Does it answer what? why? when? where? how? → ـَ
  4. Is there a preposition or an owner relationship? → ـِ
  5. Is it an adjective, or after وَ? → copy the word it follows =
